description:
Packing for a three-day trek on Mt Kenya or a weekend of camping at Hell's Gate is a different job from packing for a day hike. You need room for a sleeping bag, warm layers, food, water and a rain jacket, and you need to carry all of it for hours without your shoulders giving up. A 65L hiking backpack is built for exactly that: big enough for multi-day trips, and designed to carry the load comfortably on Kenya's steep, rough trails.

The Outlander 65L Ergonomic Rucksack is shaped to sit close to your back and spread the weight where your body handles it best. Padded shoulder straps and a hip belt move much of the load off your shoulders and onto your hips, while adjustable straps let you fine-tune the fit to your torso. Several compartments and pockets keep your gear organised, so you're not unpacking everything at camp to find your headlamp.

Why Choose This 65L Hiking Backpack?

Capacity matters most on overnight and multi-day hikes. A 65L hiking backpack holds the bulky items a smaller pack can't: a sleeping bag, an insulated jacket, a cooking set and several days of food. For most hikers, 65 litres is the sweet spot for trips of two to five days, giving enough space without encouraging you to overpack.

Comfort is the other half of the story. A heavy load carried badly causes sore shoulders, back pain and early fatigue. An ergonomic design keeps the weight close and centred, which helps your balance on loose rock and steep descents. For short outings when you don't need the space, our 28L Day Hiking Backpack is the lighter, smaller option.

Key Features

  • 65-litre capacity for overnight and multi-day trips
  • Ergonomic design that keeps the load close to your back
  • Padded shoulder straps for all-day comfort
  • Hip belt that moves weight onto your hips
  • Adjustable straps for a secure, personalised fit
  • Multiple compartments and pockets for organised packing

Benefits

Here's what a 65L hiking backpack adds to your trips:

  • Room for everything: Fit a sleeping bag, layers, food and water in one pack.
  • Less strain: The hip belt and padded straps spread the load away from your shoulders.
  • Better balance: A close, centred load keeps you steady on rocky, uneven ground.
  • Organised gear: Separate compartments make it quick to find what you need.
  • One pack for many trips: Use it for treks, camping, travel and long weekends away.

Perfect For

  • Multi-day treks and summit climbs
  • Weekend camping trips
  • Overnight hikes with a tent and sleeping bag
  • Backpacking travel and long road trips
  • Group expeditions where you carry shared gear

Where to Use a 65L Hiking Backpack in Kenya

A 65L hiking backpack comes into its own on Kenya's longer routes. On Mt Kenya, the Sirimon, Chogoria and Naro Moru routes take three to five days, and you'll carry warm layers for freezing nights at Shipton's or Mackinder's camp. Treks across the Aberdares, including Ol Donyo Lesatima, and multi-day hikes on Mt Elgon call for the same space and comfort.

It's also ideal for camping weekends at Hell's Gate, Lake Naivasha and Mt Longonot, and for longer adventures such as a Loita Hills walk or a trek across the Cherangani Hills. If you're heading across the border to climb Mt Kilimanjaro, a 65L hiking backpack is a common choice for carrying your personal gear between camps.

Packing a large rucksack well makes a big difference to comfort: heavy items should sit close to your back and between your shoulder blades, with lighter, bulky items at the bottom. You can read practical loading tips in this overview of backpacks and how they carry loads. With the right packing and a well-fitted 65L hiking backpack, even long days on the trail feel far more manageable.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a 65L hiking backpack too big for me?

For day hikes, yes, it's more than you need. For trips of two to five days, or any hike where you carry a sleeping bag and tent, 65 litres is the right size for most people.

How do I adjust it for a comfortable fit?

Load the pack first, then tighten the hip belt so it sits on your hip bones. Next, snug the shoulder straps so the pack sits close without pulling, and finish with the smaller adjustment straps. Most of the weight should rest on your hips, not your shoulders.

Can I use it for travel as well as hiking?

Yes. Many travellers use a 65L rucksack instead of a suitcase because it's easier to carry on buses, matatus and rough roads.

What should I pack for a Mt Kenya trek?

Pack a warm sleeping bag, an insulated jacket, a waterproof jacket, thermal layers, a warm hat and gloves, a headlamp and enough water. Keep your rain gear near the top so you can reach it quickly.
